newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks surge in morning on Wall Street rally.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks surge in morning on Wall Street rally.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks moved sharply higher in morning trade on Monday, as the market tool its cue from Friday's strong rally on Wall Street.
The Hang Seng Index opened on a gain of 156.90 points, or 1.20 percent, at 13,238.60 before extending its gains to rise 275.19 points, or 2.10 percent, to 13,356.89 at mid-morning.
Turnover was HK$4.60 billion after the first hour of trade.

"The market is mainly following the strength on Wall Street and interest rate sensitive banking stocks are benefiting from the declining long bond yield," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.

The Dow industrials jumped 94.72 points on Friday to 7,071.20 following the U.S. April jobs report and an agreement to balance the U.S. budget. The U.S. long bond rose 15/32, bringing the yield down to 6.88 percent.
Vickers Ballas sales director Antony Mak said the employment data had soothed concerns about higher interest rates.
The U.S. jobless rate dropped to 4.9 percent in April from 5.2 percent in March but nonfarm payrolls rose by a lower-than-expected 142,000 and average hourly earnings fell.
"The market should go higher due to the better tone to U.S. stocks," said Mak.
Shares in HSBC Holdings Plc jumped above the HK$200 level for the first time in Hong Kong, leading the market with a HK$5.50 surge to a record high of HK$203.00.
The stock had broken above HK$200 in London trading on Friday but Kwong said there could be some profit-taking later.
Hang Seng Bank Ltd was up HK$2.00 at HK$90.25 and Bank of East Asia Ltd gained HK$0.80 to HK$27.45.
Property stocks also made strong gains. Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd rose HK$2.50 to HK$73.25 and Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd added HK$2.75 to HK$90.25.

Shares in Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd fell HK$1.80 to HK$41.40. The Hong Kong Economic Times quoted a source close to the company as saying Shanghai Industrial's parent Shanghai Industrial Investment (Holdings) Co Ltd was considering lowering its stake in the company. The company denied the report.
